q: how to create a react component
how to write a react component
a: A React component is a function (or class) that returns JSX. Functional components are the modern standard. Props are passed as an argument (usually destructured). Use TypeScript for type safety with an `interface` or `type` for props. Components should be pure — given same props, return same UI. Use default exports for page components, named exports for reusable ones. File names conventionally match the component name (PascalCase).

q: how to use useState hook in react
how to manage state in react with hooks
a: `useState` returns a pair: the current state value and an updater function. State updates are asynchronous and trigger a re-render. For objects/arrays, create a new reference (don't mutate directly). The updater can take a function `prev => newValue` when the new state depends on the old. Lift shared state to the closest common ancestor. Use multiple `useState` calls for unrelated state instead of one big object.

q: how to handle events in react
how to pass parameters to event handlers in react
a: React events are named in camelCase (`onClick`, `onChange`, `onSubmit`) and receive synthetic events (cross-browser wrappers). Pass a function reference, not a call. To pass extra parameters, wrap in an arrow function or use `.bind`. For forms, use controlled components (state drives input value) or uncontrolled with `useRef`. Call `e.preventDefault()` on form submits to avoid page reload.

q: how to use useEffect hook in react
how to fetch data with useEffect
a: `useEffect` runs side effects after render. The dependency array controls when it re-runs: `[]` (once on mount), `[dep1, dep2]` (when deps change), omitted (every render). Return a cleanup function to unsubscribe, remove listeners, or cancel timers. For data fetching, handle loading/error states and include an abort controller in cleanup. `useLayoutEffect` runs synchronously before paint (use for DOM measurements). Avoid running effects unnecessarily by listing exact dependencies.

q: how to pass props in react
how to pass data from parent to child in react
a: Props flow downward from parent to child. They are read-only (immutable). Children receive props as an object; destructure them for clarity. `children` is a special prop for nested content. Use TypeScript interfaces to document props. Prop drilling (passing through many layers) is solved with composition (`children`), `React.Context`, or state management libraries. Default values can be set via destructuring defaults or `Component.defaultProps` (legacy).

q: how to conditionally render in react
a: React supports several conditional rendering patterns. Use ternary (`? :`) for inline if/else, `&&` for rendering only when true, and `if/else` outside JSX for complex logic. Guard against rendering falsy values (0, NaN) with `&&` by converting to boolean. Use early returns to avoid deep nesting. Switch between multiple components with a lookup object or `switch` statement.
